name: ghost-fields
description: GHOST FIELD ratchet. Counts `(x as any).prop` reads where `prop` is not on x's pre-cast type — a read that is `undefined` on every row, forever, with tsc explicitly told not to look. Three live defects of this shape were found by hand on 2026-08-21/23, each in a different file and none catchable by any other gate in this repo: auditOrgUsury judged EVERY note in EVERY organization against Texas usury law via `(note as any).propertyState || "TX"`; GET /api/seller-motivation/:leadId synthesized nine of eleven signals from non-existent columns and so returned at most two distinct scores across every lead in every org; and the campaign email and SMS senders read four content fields that are not columns of `campaigns`, so every recipient of every campaign received the campaign's INTERNAL NAME as the message body while `campaigns.content` went unread. Augmenting a browser/Node global (window.webkitSpeechRecognition, globalThis caches, injected window.__ENV__) is excluded BY RULE, not parked in the baseline, so this number means one thing: a domain object asked for a field it does not have. THE CHEAPEST FIX IS TO READ THE REAL FIELD, or delete the read. Widening a type to make a ghost legal is worse than the defect — it documents `undefined` as the contract.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOORS, not ratchets. The baseline counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a program that stops loading files finds zero and reports a reassuring PASS. Seeded 2026-08-23 at roughly 70% of live (644 casts in scope, 408 judged after excluding ambient globals and shapeless bases) so a broken tsconfig, scope regex or AST walk trips them while genuine cleanup does not. If a real deletion wave takes a population under its floor, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave.
lastBumpNote: 81 -> 72 on 2026-08-23, and these nine were NOT ghosts — which is the point. client/src/pages/properties.tsx carried its own `interface EnrichmentData`, a strict SUBSET of the exported one in property-enrichment-widget.tsx, missing exactly completenessScore and completenessBreakdown. Both fields are real: server/services/propertyEnrichment.ts declares completenessScore and the widget renders it. The page was receiving the data and could not see it, so nine reads cast through `as any` to work around the page's own stale copy of a type it did not need to own. Deleting the duplicate and importing the canonical type removed all nine. Recorded because it makes the remaining count harder to read, not easier: a duplicated type generates casts that look exactly like the ones hiding real defects. PRIOR NOTE — 90 -> 81 on 2026-08-23: nine reads went with the reported-financials fix. reportingEnhancements.getDealPnL read `(deal as any).salePrice` and `(deal as any).purchasePrice` — neither is a column of `deals` — so ACQUISITION, the largest cost in any deal, was always zero and the reported profit was `offerAmount * 0.95 - 200` on every deal. getCostBasisReport read `(p as any).improvementCost`, a column of no table, so every basis was reported without improvements, which overstates gain. Both now read the canonical `cost_basis` table that CostBasisTracker owns. paxEnhancements read `(prop as any).taxAssessedValue` when the real column is `assessedValue`, so Pax had never once seen a property's assessed value; and `(deal as any).askingPrice`, when the asking price is the linked property's listPrice. Spurious casts on real columns (purchasePrice, offerAmount) came out with them — a spurious `as any` beside a ghost is how the ghost survives review. PRIOR NOTE — 97 -> 90 on 2026-08-23: the seven `(invoice as any).subscription` reads across webhookHandlers.ts and stripeConnect.ts, both `invoice.payment_failed` handlers. `Invoice.subscription` does not exist in the pinned API version — Stripe moved it under parent.subscription_details — so the id was always undefined and every dunning event recorded '' for the subscription. Replaced by the canonical invoiceSubscriptionId() in stripeClient.ts. PRIOR NOTE — 100 -> 97 on 2026-08-23, the first reduction, and the gate caught it itself — it failed stale-high on the very commit that earned it, which is the behaviour the down-only rule exists for. Three reads went with the Stripe billing-period fix: `(sub as any).current_period_start` and `.current_period_end` in supportAgent (which were `new Date(NaN).toISOString()`, a RangeError on every customer who HAD a subscription) and `(sub as any).current_period_end` in paxLearning (guarded, so the renewal prediction silently never fired). A fourth site, founder-chat stripe-ops, used `as unknown as { current_period_end: number }` — a DOUBLE assertion this gate does not match, and a known limit of it. PRIOR NOTE — Seeded 2026-08-23 at the measured live count of 100. Two exclusions keep this number meaning one thing. AMBIENT bases (Window, globalThis, Document, Navigator) are excluded because augmenting a browser/Node global is a real idiom — the property genuinely is not in the ambient lib types and there is no row to read; that took 182 to 139. SHAPELESS bases (`object`, `{}`, anything with zero declared properties) are excluded because a type with no shape contradicts nothing — the cast is doing the job `any` would do; that took 139 to 100. What remains is exactly: a KNOWN shape asked for a field it does not have. A STARTING POSITION to be worked down, not an allowance.
